detail: Government accepts MediShield Life Council recommendations: expand coverage to CTGTPs assessed clinically effective and cost-effective; pilot financing framework; CTGTP coverage extension timed for October 2025.
stated_reason_verbatim: "advances in medical technologies have resulted in new, potentially life-saving therapies, such as Cell, Tissue, and Gene Therapy Products (CTGTPs), which MediShield Life also does not cover." "Expand coverage to high-cost treatments that are clinically effective and cost-effective ... CTGTPs that have demonstrated the potential to treat cancers and serious diseases effectively." "While CTGTPs have the potential to transform healthcare and treat serious diseases, they have high upfront costs. Without financing support, patients may not be able to access these potentially effective treatments. However, such financing must also be designed in a sustainable manner given the high cost of CTGTPs and uncertainty around their longer-term effectiveness. Hence the Government has introduced a pilot financing framework to focus support only on CTGTPs that have been assessed to be both clinically effective and cost-effective."

body: MOH Drug Advisory Committee / Health Technology Advisory Council / ACE
detail: Not recommended for the MOH CTGTP List (SMA, children under 2 with Type 1 SMA or up to three SMN2 copies); DAC July 2024 and March 2025, HTAC May 2025; cost-minimisation against risdiplam; about three babies born with SMA per year; cost impact SG$5-10m per year for three patients per year.
stated_reason_verbatim: "This is because the current available evidence is insufficient to show that onasemnogene abeparvovec provides superior long-term efficacy compared to risdiplam, the subsidised disease-modifying treatment for SMA. Given the current uncertainty in its superiority to risdiplam and its higher treatment cost, it is deemed that the cost-effectiveness of onasemnogene abeparvovec is unfavourable when compared to risdiplam at this time." "The CMA results showed that, at the price proposed by the company, onasemnogene abeparvovec had a higher treatment cost than risdiplam." "the price-volume agreement (PVA) proposed by the company for onasemnogene abeparvovec was inadequate to manage the uncertainty of the overall budget impact." "the cost impact to the public healthcare system was estimated to be between SG$5 million and SG$10 million per year in the first five years of including onasemnogene abeparvovec on the MOH Cell, Tissue and Gene Therapy Product (CTGTP) List for the treatment of SMA, benefitting three patients each year."
source_doc: ACE Technology Guidance: Onasemnogene abeparvovec for treating spinal muscular atrophy, published 16 Sep 2025
notes: Guidance PDF: https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/68/a59e2e11-0bb7-4d24-bca5-134fa2a9b32f/Guidance_Onasemnogene%20abeparvovec%20for%20treating%20spinal%20muscular%20atrophy%20(16%20Sep%202025).pdf . HTAC: 'onasemnogene abeparvovec offered meaningful treatment benefit for children with SMA compared to the natural history of the disease. However, they had concerns that the long-term efficacy of onasemnogene abeparvovec was uncertain'. Plain English summary: 'If your child needs onasemnogene abeparvovec for this condition, you can speak to a medical social worker to find out if there is financial assistance available'.
